text: GTA 6 is one week away. And the internet is full of gameplay facts that are just... not true.

So we went through the twenty-six minute gameplay reveal, Rockstar's own words, and every recap we could find. Thirteen myths. Let's bust them. And stay to the end, because number thirteen is going to hurt.
Myth number one. The whole map is just Vice City.
Nope. Vice City is only one part of the state of Leonida. There's the Leonida Keys, the Grassrivers wetlands, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park.
Myth number two. You can't switch between Jason and Lucia.
Switching is confirmed. When they're close, it's seamless. When they're far apart, you get a quick bird's-eye cut... and it's faster than GTA 5.
Myth number three. Stealing a car is still smash and grab.
You can still smash the window... but everybody hears it. Or you can sneak in quietly with a slim tool, like a professional.
Myth number four. People only react once you start shooting.
Walk around with a rifle out, and people notice before you fire a single shot. Lucia literally hides her pistol behind her back to stay off the radar.
Myth number five. You can rob any store in Leonida.
Convenience stores, gas stations, and phone shops are confirmed. Any store? Not confirmed. Half true.
Myth number six. Every building is enterable. Seven hundred of them.
The interiors we saw are insane. You can ride an elevator up into fully built rooms. But that seven hundred number? It comes from a leak, not from Rockstar.
Myth number seven. Cops drive unmarked cars now.
Unconfirmed. What we did see: police helicopters, shooting out tires... and the cleanest escape in the whole series. Torch the getaway car, switch to a van, change your clothes. Gone.
Myth number eight. The six-star wanted level is back.
This one depends on who you ask. One recap says a sixth star showed up on screen. Another says it's still five. We'll know in a week.
Myth number nine. Your character can get fat, like San Andreas.
True! Jason's eating and drinking change his weight... and Lucia can hit the bench press and build muscle. CJ would be proud.
Myth number ten. There are alligators.
Also true. The Grassrivers wetlands have alligators. And Mount Kalaga has hunting and fishing. Florida... stays Florida.
Myth number eleven. The phone is just a menu.
Nope. It runs real social media feeds, and whole storylines play out in the posts... like the rise of the rap duo Real Dimez.
Myth number twelve. It runs at sixty frames per second on PS5.
Probably not at launch. Co-director Rob Nelson reportedly said it's targeting thirty frames per second on every console. A sixty F-P-S mode? Still being decided.
And myth number thirteen. The one that hurts. GTA Online launches on day one.
It doesn't. On November nineteenth, GTA 6 is a single-player game, and there's no online date yet. For history: GTA Online came two weeks after GTA 5. Red Dead Online? Seven months.
So, which one fooled you? Tell me in the comments. GTA 6 drops November nineteenth, and the second it's out, we're checking every single one of these. Subscribe, so you don't miss it.
